subject: Toolsmith SDK adapter deprecation & compatibility plan
messages:
From: Rajesh Patel <rajesh@toolsmith.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Toolsmith Labs Platform Team <platform@toolsmith.com>
Date: Mon, 4 Jun 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: SDK adapter deprecation notice — compatibility ask

Marcus,

Quick heads-up from our side — engineering has scheduled removal of our legacy SDK adapter (v1.x) from the Toolsmith distribution in Q3, target week of 2028-08-12. This adapter is how several ISVs (including a couple of your mutual customers) integrate with Redwood’s hosted endpoints.

Before we lock the date, we wanted to check whether Redwood can commit to one of two options:

- Provide a thin compatibility shim on the Redwood side that accepts v1.x adapter behavior for 12 months post-deprecation, or
- Offer a short-term compatibility policy (3 months) plus a clear migration path and SDK tests we can run pre-cutover.

Attached: toolsmith-deprecation-request.docx (request letter + customer list).

High-level asks from Toolsmith:
- Estimated engineering effort and timeline from Redwood for a shim (if feasible)
- Any constraints around streaming/payloads we should be aware of
- Proposed rollback/canary strategy to minimize customer impact

Can you loop in the right people on your side? We’d like to align on an MAP and a joint comms plan to customers.

Thanks,
Rajesh
Head of Platform Partnerships
Toolsmith Labs

-----

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 4 Jun 2028 09:29:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: SDK adapter deprecation notice — compatibility ask

Forwarding Rajesh’s note — short summary:
- Toolsmith is planning to remove their v1 adapter in August; several mutual customers will be impacted.
- They want either a Redwood-side shim (12 months) or a short-term policy + migration tests.

Can we get a quick feasibility read from engineering and product? Specifics I need:
1) Rough effort estimate for a compatibility shim (kernels/serving/runtime impact)
2) Whether streaming and chunked responses complicate a shim (especially for stateful adapters)
3) Canary/rollout approach we can recommend to Toolsmith and customers

Cc’ing Grace for comms + MAP work. I can join a call with Rajesh later this week.

Thanks — Marcus
Account Executive, Strategic Partners
Redwood Inference

-----

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Rajesh Patel <rajesh@toolsmith.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 4 Jun 2028 13:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SDK adapter deprecation notice — compatibility ask

Rajesh — thanks for the heads-up and the attachment. I dug into the ask with runtime and infra. Key takeaways below (TL;DR: shim is feasible but with caveats).

Quoted for context:
> Marcus,
> 
> Quick heads-up from our side — engineering has scheduled removal of our legacy SDK adapter (v1.x) from the Toolsmith distribution in Q3, target week of 2028-08-12.
> 
> Before we lock the date, we wanted to check whether Redwood can commit to one of two options: provide a thin compatibility shim on the Redwood side that accepts v1.x adapter behavior for 12 months post-deprecation, or offer a short-term compatibility policy (3 months) plus a clear migration path and SDK tests we can run pre-cutover.

Proposed Redwood approach (high level):
- Short-term (target: 6–9 weeks): deliver a compatibility adapter layer in front of the serving runtime that translates v1.x adapter calls to the current API surface. This will be a lightweight translation layer (no model changes).
- Medium-term (3–6 months): publish migration SDK helpers, automated tests (compat-test-matrix.csv), and a customer-facing migration guide.
- Canary & rollback: recommend a staged canary by customer segment with feature-flag gating and automatic failover to the current adapter if we detect parity or latency regressions.

Known constraints and risks:
- Streaming semantics: v1.x uses a different framing for partial tokens in some SDKs; the shim will normalize at token/sequence boundaries which could introduce minor ordering differences for a very small subset of workloads. We’ll document this in the migration guide.
- Performance: expected P95 token latency could increase by ~5–12% under heavy concurrency for shimmed requests; we can mitigate with autoscaling policies for affected pools.
- Test coverage: we’ll need Toolsmith to provide representative request traces and the customer list to build the compat-test-matrix.csv.

Attachments: toolsmith-shim-proposal-v1.pdf (technical design), compat-test-matrix.csv (schema + example entries)

Next steps I propose:
1) Joint scoping call (30m) this week to agree on scope and major milestones — Marcus/Grace can pick slots.
2) Toolsmith to share 2–3 customer request traces and a priority customer list for canary staging.
3) Redwood to deliver an internal impact estimate and a first-cut shim prototype in ~6 weeks.

If that sounds OK I’ll schedule the call and share the technical docs.

— Soojin
Director, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

-----

From: Rajesh Patel <rajesh@toolsmith.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 5 Jun 2028 08:21:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SDK adapter deprecation notice — compatibility ask

Thanks Soojin — that plan is helpful and broadly acceptable. A couple quick clarifying Qs before the call:
- For the streaming framing differences, can you estimate customer-visible impact (examples: partial token duplication, out-of-order partial events)?
- On the customer traces — we can share sanitized traces for up to 5 customers in the high-priority list. Do you also need sampling parameters?

We’d like to avoid a 12-month open-ended shim if possible; our preference is a well-defined 6–9 week shim with a firm sunset communicated in the MAP and a 6-month deprecation window post-cutover.

Happy to join a scoping call Thursday morning (our time).

— Rajesh

-----

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Rajesh Patel <rajesh@toolsmith.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 6 Jun 2028 16:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SDK adapter deprecation notice — compatibility ask

Rajesh — excellent, thanks for the quick reply and the preference guidance. From a partner ops / MAP perspective we’ll do the following: 

- Schedule a scoping call Thu 2028-06-08 10:00 PT / 13:00 ET — calendar invite & agenda (includes goals, timelines, customer list ask, and comms draft).
- Redwood will prepare the canary plan (canary-rollout-plan.md) and a short comms template that Toolsmith can use to notify impacted customers.
- We agree to aim for a 6–9 week shim delivery with a 6-month sunset window post-cutover. We’ll surface firm SLAs if we need to extend beyond that.

Action items:
- Toolsmith: share sanitized traces + priority customer list before the call (Rajesh).
- Redwood (Soojin): prototype shim + compat-test-matrix.csv by 2028-07-15.
- Redwood (Grace): draft MAP & customer comms by 2028-06-13.

Attachments: canary-rollout-plan.md

Looking forward to the call — Marcus, please add any stakeholders on your side.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Partner Operations Lead
Redwood Inference
